BLOCKER: Acceptance criteria require the /memory API to accept a `user` parameter, but `memoryHandle` GET hardcodes `User: principal` (env `PF_MEMORY_PRINCIPAL`); there is no `user` query param, so per-user ACL filtering is unreachable at the API and the AC's "user" contract is unimplemented.

All entries posted through the API get `Owner = env principal` (default "admin"), so the eight-type ACL model (private-per-owner) is effectively single-principal in production; the negative tests only exercise it via direct `MemoryStore` calls, not the shipped API.
MAJOR: `Put` silently discards the embedding when pgvector is absent (no log, no error, no signal in the response); callers reasonably believe the vector was persisted — data loss without observability.

Backward-compat break: legacy `?kind=X` previously filtered `kind = X` exactly (old `q` was compared to the kind column); it is now a free-text FTS query, so existing clients filtering by kind silently get different results.
Hybrid queries add `embedding IS NOT NULL` to WHERE, so supplying a vector silently hides every entry that lacks an embedding — scope-limited result sets without documentation or test coverage.

AC requires "integration tests plus unit tests": `memory_test.go` contains only DSN-gated integration tests (skipped in default CI) — no unit tests for `formatVector`, kind/ACL validation, or embedding dimension checks; the claimed hybrid/FTS-only degradation test with a valid 1536-dim vector is also absent.

Migration 0015 adds a `GENERATED ALWAYS ... STORED` tsvector column, which forces a full table rewrite; combined with `SET LOCAL lock_timeout='5s'` (a no-op if the runner executes the file outside a transaction) this can abort the migration on any non-trivial `memory` table.
MINOR: `formatVector` uses `%g` (6 significant digits) for float32 vectors, discarding ~3 digits of precision per component and degrading cosine ranking; NaN/Inf also serialize to non-pgvector-safe literals.
`Search` applies the explicit tenant guard only `if scope.TenantID != ""`; an empty tenant falls back entirely to RLS instead of failing closed as the AC's "RLS plus explicit guard" implies.
The cross-tenant negative test is masked: `store.BindTenant(st, tenant)` makes RLS return zero rows regardless of the explicit `tenant_id` predicate, so it doesn't prove the code-level guard.
Put accepts an empty `Kind` (validation only rejects non-empty unknown kinds) and surfaces the DB CHECK violation as HTTP 500 instead of 400; same for DB-level ACL violations.

Observability: `log.Printf` in library code, unstructured error strings, no metrics/logging for FTS-only degradation, search latency, or result counts; `memoryByID` collapses all `Get` errors to 404 with no logging.
Legacy `source` values are heuristically remapped when they equal ACL names ("private"/"project"/...); a genuine source literally named "private" is silently reinterpreted as an ACL filter.
Upsert `WHERE ... memory.owner = EXCLUDED.owner` makes a legitimate re-PUT by a different principal fail with a 500 that conflates tenant and owner conflicts.
NIT: `EmbeddingDim = 1536` is duplicated as a literal `vector(1536)` in the migration — no single source of truth for the vector contract.
`where := []string{"TRUE"}` and the conditional `ORDER BY` string building are awkward; a builder or always-parameterized rank expression would be clearer.
The returned `Score` (0.7/0.3 blend) is serialized straight to API clients, leaking an internal ranking heuristic as public contract.

Down migration intentionally keeps data but also leaves `memory_kind_valid`/`memory_acl_valid` constraints and never drops `content/source/owner/embedding`, so rollback leaves schema drift from the pre-0015 state.
SUMMARY: Solid substrate direction (parameterized FTS-first SQL, server-side ACL predicates, optional-pgvector migration, RLS + guard), and the language rule (Go) is respected, but the AC's API contract (`user` param, per-owner principal) is not actually implemented in the shipped handler.
Top risks: silent embedding drop on Put, changed `?kind=` semantics breaking existing clients, vector queries hiding non-embedded rows, and a migration that can lock/rewrite the table.
Verification is weaker than claimed: no unit tests, no valid-dimension degradation test, and the cross-tenant negative is masked by RLS — precheck PASS should not be read as AC coverage.
